questions.question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹ 531 for a period of 5 years at the rate of 9% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 5 years = 9% × 5 = 45%.

Let the principal amount be 100%.

According to the question, 45% of Principal = ₹531.

1% of Principal = 531 ÷ 45 = 11.8

100% of Principal = 11.8 × 100 = 1180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (I) = ₹531

Time (T) = 5 years

Rate (R) = 9% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 Year 0
 P = ?
 
 
 Year 5
 
 

 Total SI = ₹531
 
 
 Rate = 9% p.a.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 531 = (P × 9 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 531 = (P × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (531 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ P = 53100 ÷ 45

⇒ P = 1180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Amount

The total amount after T years is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest. Formula: A = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest. Formula: A = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years on a given principal is calculated as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: The population of a town increases by 8% annually. If the present population is 45,000, what will be its population after 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective percentage increase for 2 successive years = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective increase = 8 + 8 + (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16.64%

⇒ Population after 2 years = Initial Population × (100% + 16.64%)

⇒ Population after 2 years = 45000 × 116.64% = 450 × 116.64 = 52,488

**∴ The correct answer is 52,488.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Population (P) = 45,000

Rate of increase (R) = 8%

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Population after T years = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

questions.question: 400 guavas were bought at ₹ 1240 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹ 940. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of guavas.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) for 400 guavas = 4 × ₹1240 = ₹4960

Total Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 4960 + 940 = ₹5900

SP of 1 guava = 5900 ÷ 400 = ₹59/4

Selling price per dozen (12 guavas) = (59/4) × 12 = 59 × 3 = ₹177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of guavas bought = 400

Cost rate = ₹1240 per 100 guavas

Profit earned = ₹940

**Formula Used:**

Total Selling Price (SP) = Total Cost Price (CP) + Profit

SP per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total Quantity) × 12

 
 
 

 
 
 
 Total CP = ₹4960
 

 + ₹940 Profit
 
 Total SP = ₹5900
 Transaction for 400 Guavas

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP for 400 guavas = (1240 ÷ 100) × 400

⇒ Total CP = 1240 × 4 = ₹4960

⇒ Total SP for 400 guavas = 4960 + 940 = ₹5900

⇒ Number of dozens in 400 guavas = 400 ÷ 12 = 100/3 dozens

⇒ SP of 1 dozen = Total SP ÷ Total dozens

⇒ SP of 1 dozen = 5900 ÷ (100/3)

⇒ SP of 1 dozen = (5900 × 3) ÷ 100 = 59 × 3 = ₹177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Formula: Profit = SP − CP.

Unitary Method

The Unitary Method involves finding the value of a single unit first, and then multiplying it to find the total value for the required units.

Quantity Conversion

One dozen consists of 12 items. To convert a per-item price to a per-dozen price, simply multiply the price of one item by 12.

questions.question: The height of a right circular cone is 10 cm and its base radius is 24 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm²) of the cone?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The radius (24) and height (10) form a Pythagorean triplet with the slant height (l).

Triplet base (5, 12, 13) × 2 → (10, 24, 26). Thus, slant height l = 26 cm.

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l

CSA = π × 24 × 26 = 624π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 624π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 24 cm

Height of the cone (h) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π × r × l

 

 

 
• 
 
• 
 

 h = 10
 r = 24
 l = ?
 Curved Surface Area = πrl

**Calculations:**

⇒ l = √(24² + 10²)

⇒ l = √(576 + 100)

⇒ l = √676

⇒ l = 26 cm

⇒ CSA = π × 24 × 26

⇒ CSA = 624π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 624π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

TSA includes both the curved surface and the circular base: TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The space occupied by the cone is given by: V = (1/3) × πr²h.

Frustum of a Cone

When the top of a cone is sliced off parallel to the base, the curved surface area of the resulting frustum is πl(r₁ + r₂).
</p

questions.question: The marked price of a table is ₹ 8,980. If the shopkeeper offers a discount of 19%, what is its selling price (in ₹, to the nearest rupee)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Selling Price (SP) will be exactly (100% − 19%) = 81% of the Marked Price.

SP = 81% of 8980

SP = 0.81 × 8980 = 7273.8

Rounding off to the nearest rupee, we get ₹ 7,274.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 7,274.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹ 8,980

Discount = 19%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 MP
 ₹ 8980
 
 

 − 19% Discount
 
 
 SP
 ₹ 7274

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 8980 × (100 − 19) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 8980 × 81 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 898 × 8.1

⇒ SP = 7273.8

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest rupee, SP ≈ ₹ 7,274

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 7,274.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated by: a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Mark-up Percentage

It is the percentage by which the Marked Price is set above the Cost Price. Formula: Mark-up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

Direct Relation (MP and CP)

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly written as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

questions.question: When 8, 16, 18, 20 and 25 divide the least number x, the remainder in each case is 3, but x is divisible by 7. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be of the form [LCM(8, 16, 18, 20, 25) × k] + 3.

LCM of the given divisors is 3600, so the number x = 3600k + 3.

Since x is exactly divisible by 7, (3600k + 3) ÷ 7 must yield a remainder of 0.

3600 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 2, so we only need to check the remainder of (2k + 3).

For k = 2, 2(2) + 3 = 7, which is fully divisible by 7. Thus, x = 3600 × 2 + 3 = 7203.

**∴ The correct answer is 7203.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 8, 16, 18, 20 and 25

Remainder in each case = 3

The number x is exactly divisible by 7.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = LCM(Divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorization of the given divisors:

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 16 = 2⁴

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ 25 = 5²

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3² × 5²

⇒ LCM = 16 × 9 × 25 = 3600

⇒ Therefore, the required least number x is of the form 3600k + 3.

⇒ We are given that x is exactly divisible by 7.

⇒ 3600k + 3 = (514 × 7 + 2)k + 3

⇒ 3600k + 3 = 7 × 514k + (2k + 3)

⇒ For the entire expression to be completely divisible by 7, the remaining term (2k + 3) must be a multiple of 7.

⇒ Put k = 1: 2(1) + 3 = 5 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ Put k = 2: 2(2) + 3 = 7 (Exactly divisible by 7)

⇒ Substitute k = 2 into the general expression for x:

⇒ x = 3600 × 2 + 3

⇒ x = 7200 + 3 = 7203

**∴ The correct answer is 7203.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves the same remainder r in each case, the required least number is given by LCM(a, b, c) × k + r.

LCM Remainder Concept (Different Remainders)

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders p, q, and r respectively such that (a − p) = (b − q) = (c − r) = d, the required number is LCM(a, b, c) × k − d.

HCF Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

The greatest number that divides a, b, and c to leave the same remainder in each case is the HCF of |a − b|, |b − c|, and |c − a|.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is exactly 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.
</p

questions.question: Baban has two grandsons Rakesh and Shivam. 13 year old Rakesh gets some money from Baban’s wealth and 14 year old Shivam gets rest of the money. But Rakesh and Shivam will get money only when they turn 22 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 10% compounded annually. When both turn 22, they receive the same amount. How much had Baban given Shivam (in ₹) initially, if total money with Baban was ₹ 23100?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When CI amounts become equal, the ratio of shares is (1 + Rate/100)Time Diff.

Difference in time = (22 − 13) − (22 − 14) = 9 − 8 = 1 year.

Ratio of Shivam's share to Rakesh's share = (1 + 10/100)¹ = 11/10.

Shivam's share = [11 ÷ (11 + 10)] × 23100 = (11/21) × 23100.

Shivam's share = 11 × 1100 = 12100.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money = ₹23100

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Rakesh's age = 13 years, Shivam's age = 14 years

Final amounts at age 22 are equal

**Formula Used:**

Amount in CI = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
• 
 
 
 Age 13
 ₹ R
 Age 22
 Amount A
 9 years @ 10% CI
 
 
• 
 
 
 Age 14
 ₹ S
 Age 22
 Amount A
 8 years @ 10% CI
 
 

 Equal Amounts

**Calculations:**

Let the initial amount given to Rakesh be ₹R and to Shivam be ₹S.

⇒ Total sum = R + S = 23100

⇒ Time for Rakesh's sum to grow = 22 − 13 = 9 years

⇒ Time for Shivam's sum to grow = 22 − 14 = 8 years

⇒ Amount of Rakesh = Amount of Shivam

⇒ R(1 + 10/100)⁹ = S(1 + 10/100)⁸

⇒ R(1.1)⁹ = S(1.1)⁸

⇒ R × 1.1 = S

⇒ S/R = 1.1/1 = 11/10

⇒ Ratio of Shivam's share to Rakesh's share = 11 : 10

⇒ Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21

⇒ 21 parts = 23100

⇒ 1 part = 23100 ÷ 21 = 1100

⇒ Shivam's share (11 parts) = 11 × 1100 = 12100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division of Sum in Compound Interest

When a sum is divided such that amounts on two parts are equal after different times (t₁ and t₂), the ratio of the principal parts is inversely proportional to the accumulating factor: P₁/P₂ = (1 + r/100)t² − t¹.

Compound Interest Formula

The amount accumulated after n years is calculated as A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, and the Compound Interest earned is CI = A − P.

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For 2 years, the effective rate of CI is given by Rₑff = 2R + (R²/100)%. This helps in finding direct percentage change without calculating the final amount first.

questions.question: Zakir travels from City A to City B. If Zakir drives his car at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 45 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Zakir would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (New : Normal) = 2 : 3

Time ratio (New : Normal) = 3 : 2 (since distance is constant)

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

1 unit = 45 minutes

Normal time (2 units) = 2 × 45 = 90 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 90 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 2/3 of normal speed

Zakir is late by 45 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When Distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 / Time

 
• 
 
 
 City A
 City B
 Distance (D) = Constant
 Normal Journey: Speed = S, Time = T
 New Journey: Speed = 2/3 S, Time = T + 45

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ Normal Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = (2/3) × S

⇒ Since the distance is the same, New Time = (3/2) × T

⇒ We are given that the new time is 45 minutes more than the normal time.

⇒ New Time − Normal Time = 45 minutes

⇒ (3/2 × T) − T = 45

⇒ (1/2) × T = 45

⇒ T = 90 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 90 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

If equal distances are covered at different speeds, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂). Otherwise, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Inverse Proportionality

If distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional (S₁ / S₂ = T₂ / T₁).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: Find the ratio in which rice at ₹ 8.30 per kg be mixed with rice at ₹ 5.30 per kg to produce a mixture worth ₹ 6.30 per kg.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct Alligation cross method for the two varieties:

Ratio of quantity of dearer to cheaper rice = (Mean Price − Cheaper Price) : (Dearer Price − Mean Price)

⇒ Ratio = (6.30 − 5.30) : (8.30 − 6.30)

⇒ Ratio = 1.00 : 2.00 = 1 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of dearer rice (D) = ₹ 8.30 per kg

Price of cheaper rice (C) = ₹ 5.30 per kg

Mean price of the mixture (M) = ₹ 6.30 per kg

questions.question: A scooterist is travelling at the speed of 42 km/h. How much distance (in km) will they travel in 90 minutes?

Distance is the product of speed and time.

Time in hours = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours.

Distance = 42 × 1.5 = 63 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 63 km.**

questions.question: The average weight of Amit, Gopal and Akshay is 45 kg. If the average weight of Amit and Gopal be 43 kg and that of Gopal and Akshay be 47 kg, then the weight of Gopal (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall average of the 3 persons = 45 kg

Deviation of (Amit + Gopal) average from overall = (43 − 45) × 2 = −4 kg

Deviation of (Gopal + Akshay) average from overall = (47 − 45) × 2 = +4 kg

Weight of the overlapping person (Gopal) = Overall Average + Sum of Deviations

⇒ Gopal's weight = 45 + (−4 + 4) = 45 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 45 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Amit, Gopal, and Akshay = 45 kg

Average weight of Amit and Gopal = 43 kg

Average weight of Gopal and Akshay = 47 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of Persons

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of weights of Amit, Gopal, and Akshay = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

⇒ Sum of weights of Amit and Gopal = 43 × 2 = 86 kg

⇒ Sum of weights of Gopal and Akshay = 47 × 2 = 94 kg

⇒ Adding the weights of the two sub-groups:

⇒ (Amit + Gopal) + (Gopal + Akshay) = 86 + 94

⇒ Amit + 2 × Gopal + Akshay = 180 kg

⇒ Subtracting the total weight of all three from this sum gives Gopal's weight:

⇒ Gopal's weight = 180 − 135

⇒ Gopal's weight = 45 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 45 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overlapping Group Averages

When one individual is counted twice in two separate sub-groups, their value can be found by: Overlapping Value = (Sum of Group 1 + Sum of Group 2) − Total Sum of all elements.

Deviation Method for Averages

The sum of deviations of all elements from their mean is always zero. This allows for quick calculation of missing values by balancing the positive and negative deviations across given groups.

Weighted Average

When groups have different numbers of items and different averages, the combined average is calculated as: (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: Three persons step out together for a walk. Their steps measure 90 cm, 95 cm and 75 cm, respectively. What is the minimum distance (in m) each should walk so that they can cover the distance in complete step?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The minimum distance covered in complete steps is the LCM of the individual step lengths (90 cm, 95 cm, and 75 cm).

Take the common factor 5 out: LCM = 5 × LCM(18, 19, 15)

Since 18 and 15 have LCM 90, LCM(18, 19, 15) = 90 × 19 = 1710

Total distance (LCM) = 5 × 1710 = 8550 cm.

Convert to meters: 8550 cm ÷ 100 = 85.5 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 85.5 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Step measure of 1st person = 90 cm

Step measure of 2nd person = 95 cm

Step measure of 3rd person = 75 cm

**Concept Used:**

To find the minimum distance covered in complete steps by all persons, we must calculate the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their given step measures.

questions.question: P and Q can do a piece of work in 10, and 6 days, respectively, while R can destroy the same work in 15 days. If P and Q work on 1st day, R works on 2ⁿd and so on. They follow the same pattern until the work gets completed. How many days will it take for the work to be completed the first time?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(10, 6, 15) = 30 units.

Combined cycle of 2 days (P+Q then R) = (3 + 5) − 2 = 6 units.

Work done in 4 cycles (8 days) = 4 × 6 = 24 units.

Remaining 6 units are completed by P & Q on the 9th day in 6 ÷ 8 = 3/4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 ³/₄ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 10 days

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 6 days

Time taken by R to destroy the work = 15 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in 1st day by P and Q = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

⇒ Work done in 2ⁿd day by R = −2 units.

⇒ Total work done in a cycle of 2 days = 8 − 2 = 6 units.

⇒ Work done in 4 cycles (8 days) = 4 × 6 = 24 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 30 − 24 = 6 units.

⇒ On the 9th day, P and Q will work. Their combined efficiency is 8 units/day.

⇒ Time taken to complete the remaining 6 units = 6 ÷ 8 = 3/4 days.

⇒ Total time taken = 8 + 3/4 = 8 ³/₄ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 ³/₄ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Days Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle. Always check the peak positive work in the cycle so you do not over-calculate cycles beyond the required total work.

Negative Work (Pipes & Cisterns concept)

When someone destroys work, their efficiency is taken as negative. The total cycle efficiency is the sum of positive and negative efficiencies.

LCM Method for Time & Work

Total work is assumed to be the LCM of individual times. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken.

questions.question: A man sold an article for ₹ 35,400 and made a profit of 18% in the process. What would have been his profit or loss percentage, had he sold it for ₹ 33,000?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling price of ₹35,400 corresponds to 118% of Cost Price.

⇒ Equivalent percentage for ₹33,000 = (118 ÷ 35,400) × 33,000

⇒ Equivalent percentage = (1 ÷ 300) × 33,000 = 110%

⇒ Since 110% is 10% more than 100% (Cost Price), there is a gain of 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is Gain 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹35,400

Initial Profit% = 18%

New Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹33,000

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (35,400 × 100) ÷ (100 + 18)

⇒ CP = (35,400 × 100) ÷ 118

⇒ CP = 300 × 100 = ₹30,000

⇒ Profit = New SP − CP = 33,000 − 30,000 = ₹3,000

⇒ Profit% = (3,000 ÷ 30,000) × 100

⇒ Profit% = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is Gain 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price.

Successive Profit or Loss

Net change% = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. For a loss, substitute the percentage value with a negative sign.

Dishonest Dealer

Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100 when a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses faulty weights.

questions.question: The expenditure of Sudha is 175% more than her savings. If her expenditure decreases by 12% and savings increase by 40.5%, then by what percent does her income increase?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = 275 : 100 = 11 : 4, Total Income parts = 15.

Using net deviation: % Change = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂)

⇒ Net % Change = [(11 × −12) + (4 × 40.5)] ÷ 15

⇒ Net % Change = [−132 + 162] ÷ 15 = 30 ÷ 15 = +2%

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

**Given:**

Expenditure is 175% more than savings.

Expenditure decreases by 12% and savings increase by 40.5%.
